articleTitle: Implementation of Hardware Trace Buffer Module for RISC-V Processor Core
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: Debugging of modern embedded systems can be very challenging due to the close cooperation of many independent components they consist of. The necessity to maintain timing dependencies during the debugging process of one component requires using non-intrusive methods, such as instruction tracing. In this paper we present a Verilog RTL implementation of a trace buffer module for a single-issue RISC-V processor. Our trace buffer is capable of adapting signals available in processor core to make any single-issue RISC- V processor compatible with the encoder interface. The system produces and saves enough data to reproduce the program flow based on the collected data, the program binary and firmware source code. The generated data packets are stored inside the internal FIFO buffer that can be reached through the configuration and status register interface, as well as passed to the transport layer. The implementation follows the Efficient Trace for RISC- V specification. The implemented module has been functionally verified including RISC- V reference test vectors. The design was synthesized with Yosys synthesis tool and FreePDK 45nm standard cell library.

articleTitle: A 0.006 mm2 Low Input Capacitance Low Power Fully Differential Neural Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: Neural amplifiers are desired to have ultra low power, low noise, low area, high input impedance, band pass response and high CMRR. Capacitively coupled instrumentation amplifier (CCIA) is a widely used topology as it features high power efficiency and moderate area, CMRR and input impedance. The main idea of area minimization relies on the minimum value implementation of the feedback capacitor of the CCIA and optimum mid band gain. We have proposed a feedback network which gives better mismatch for a given equivalent feedback capacitor which allows us to minimize the feedback capacitance without degrading the CMRR and gain mismatch. The amplifier implemented in 180 nm CMOS technology has among the lowest reported area of 0.006 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mm^{2}$</tex> and has an input capacitance of 1 pF. The amplifier consumes 1.08 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu W$</tex> of power and has an NEF of 5.2 with input referred noise of 12.4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu V$</tex> in 1 – 5 KHz bandwidth. The post layout simulation results of the amplifier are presented.

articleTitle: Modeling and Comparing the Impact of Resistive and Capacitive Crossbar Associated Parasitics of Neuromorphic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: Neuro-inspired computing systems have shown a promising future in artificial intelligence. To meet the performance requirement of neuro-inspired computing systems, various synaptic devices are being used to store the weights. Resistive synapses have been in focus, but recently, capacitive synapses have emerged as a potential candidate for the synaptic device. Increasing complexity in a neuromorphic system causes the interconnect parasitics to significantly affect the circuit's performance. Therefore, this paper provides a comprehensive study on how the resistive and capacitive synapse-based crossbar parasitics affect the performance of the system. To extract the parasitic components, a Q3D model is designed considering both the resistive and capacitive synapses. A complete crossbar-associated parasitics architecture is designed that can be used to analyze the crossbar of any dimension. The analysis is done to compare the parasitic effect of both the resistive and capacitive synapses on different spiking patterns of the Izhikevich neuron for different crossbar sizes. Based on the results, the capacitive synapse-based crossbar array outperforms the resistive synapse in terms of reduced signal distortion and delay. The circuit implementation is done using 180 nm standard CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Influence of Parasitic Capacitances and Inductances in a Power Electronic Converter on Junction Temperature of Power GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: GaN HEMTs are increasingly popular in power electronics applications. Their main advantage over other power semiconductor devices is low switching losses. However, it makes them also more sensitive to parasitic inductances and capacitances occurring in the circuit. They not only influence the waveforms of terminal currents and voltages by introducing overvoltages and overcurrents but also switching losses and, consequently, junction temperature. In the paper, the influence of parasitic elements occurring in the circuit on the junction temperature of GaN HEMTs operating in synchronous buck DC-DC converter is presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Hardware Acceleration Method Using RISC-V Core with No ISA Extensions
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: We propose a method for hardware acceleration of different algorithms using a specially designed RISC-V core. Acceleration is handled by only CSR registers without adding any new instruction to the Instruction Set Architecture (ISA). The core microarchitecture was extended and it operates in several modes, which allow to speed up the code being executed. The core modification is a general purpose and can be applied to other cores. To be able to use the processor operating modes, the assembly code must be appropriately modified, as shown in the example of calculating the Number Theoretic-Transform (NTT). Thanks to such hardware/software approach we were able to reduce the number of cycles of the Kyber NTT algorithm by 30% compared to the optimized assembly program.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Battery Charge and Discharge Protection Circuit for Bio-Implantable Sensors in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper proposes an ultra-low power complete battery protection circuit with key four features to avoid battery malfunction and damage during charging and discharging modes for bio-implantable battery-powered sensors. The protection circuit is complemented by a recovery capability managed by a biasing approach in charging and discharging mode, ensuring the recovery of a fully depleted battery and disconnected protection circuits for cold start conditions. The charger part of the circuit connects the battery to the energy harvester while avoiding over-voltage and under-voltage charging by providing a safe narrow charging window of 4 V to 4.2 V and consuming only 460 pW in 65 nm standard CMOS technology in post-layout simulation. The low-power discharge protection circuits, consuming 520 pW, disconnect the battery from both continuous and switching loads to avoid full depletion of the battery. The fourth protective feature is provided by an ultra-low power, 80 pW, deep-sleep protection circuit extending the integrated battery-powered sensor storage time from a week to a month avoiding battery replacement after a long period of inactivity.

articleTitle: Limitations in the Transmission Line and High Power Rate Race Combiners Used in SSPA 450W CW Amplifiers in the C Band
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: The article presents power summing on the example of a microwave amplifier operating in the 4.4÷5 GHz band, implemented on GAN HEMT transistors. The output power of 400 W CW was obtained by summing four modules of a multi-stage 125 W amplifier using Rate-Race combiners implemented in coaxial line technology as well as a Magic-T waveguide combiner. The temperature phenomena that appeared when summing the output power for a continuous wave (CW) signal were described. The amplifier is designed in class A to obtain low values of EVM parameters while maintaining output power and efficiency.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Circuit with Applications in Analog Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: We will present a new approach of designing analog signal processing circuits, introducing the new concept of multifunctional structures (computational circuits based on the re-using of the same functional core for obtaining multiple linear and nonlinear circuit functions). The efficiency of the proposed design technique will be illustrated for obtaining high performances fundamental analog signal processing circuits: highly linear differential amplifiers and squaring blocks. The advantages of using this approach of designing analog signal processing structures are mainly related to the very important reducing of circuit complexity and accuracy for each developed circuit function. The circuits are designed for low-voltage low-power operations, being supplied at 0.7V and consuming between 0.3uA and 0.9uA. They allow extremely large amplitude of the input signal (between -800mV and 800mV), being able to obtain a very good accuracy of circuit functions implementations. The estimated theoretical results are confirmed by specific simulations, showing an excellent accuracy, correlated with a low-voltage low-power operation.

articleTitle: Ethernet APL Survey and Application
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: The Ethernet APL is an evolution of Physical Layers in communication of Industrial Networks. This paper presents the description and applications of this physical layer, evaluating the historical context of its implementation, as its available functionalities, and the capability to operate in hazardous areas and the ability to work with various industrial network protocols based on Ethernet as PROFINET. Furthermore, it is also discussed the expansion of Ethernet networks in the industrial environment.

articleTitle: Utilizing Deep Learning Techniques to Eliminate the Current Sensor in a Boost Converter Used in a DC Nano-Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper investigates the control structure without a current sensor in a boost DC-DC converter used in a DC Nano-grid, including a photovoltaic (PV) array. Instead of the current sensor, a PV array output current prediction system based on a deep neural network is used. There are three main factors in determining the accuracy of the discussed neural network: the number and type of data required for neural network training, neural network architecture, and its training algorithm. The input data will be processed and standardized in the discussed system before being applied to the neural network. Multi-layer feedforward architecture has been used to build the neural network model, consisting of one input layer including nine important features, six hidden layers, and one output layer. Adam's optimization algorithm is also used to minimize the Loss function. All forecasting steps, including data processing, neural network model building, and its training, have been done in the Jupyter lab environment of Python programming language. The obtained results indicate the system's successful performance, and the r2_score evaluation criterion, which is used to measure the accuracy of the prediction, has been calculated and provides acceptable results.

articleTitle: Dry Electrodes for Capturing Brain Electrical Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: Almost a hundred years ago, in 1924, the first electroencephalogram - EEG, recording of brain electrical activity, was conducted by placing a metal electrode over the scalp with a conductive electrolytic gel. The electrode was connected to a signal amplifier and a signal recorder. Over the years, there has been great improvements in EEG equipments, including integrated circuits that can offer amplification, filtering and even the measurement of electrode contact impedance. However, only after the 1990s, new types of electrodes were considered to replace the traditional electrodes that requires gel, such as the dry electrodes. There are several models of dry electrodes, but they have not yet found a model that is fully accepted among clinicians. In this article we provide an overview of the current dry electrode technologies.

articleTitle: Improving Accuracy of the Current Mirrors for High-Resolution Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a reliable approach to remove mismatch of the current sources in the current-mode DACs. Specifically, design of a novel dynamic single-stage current-mode comparator with an offset cancellation mechanism based on the bulk-controlled technique, is presented. The study focuses on the application of this concept to a 4-bit current-mode DAC for the sake of simplicity. Simulation results through HSPICE in a standard 0.18 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> CMOS technology prove that not only the proposed structure is capable to provide high-resolution currents for applying on the current-mode DACs, but also generates more accurate currents for high resolution applications such as image sensors and analog to digital converters. Notably, the total power consumption of the proposed structure is 140 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{W}$</tex> with the power supply of 1.8 V. Furthermore, the proposed offset cancellation circuit demonstrates a settling time of 1.6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{s}$</tex> and occupies a compact active area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30\times 34\mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex>, make it suitable to integration with highly compact circuits as well as practical implementations.

articleTitle: Management of Renewable Generation with Storage Energy Connect to the Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: Battery Energy Storage Systems - BESS and other forms of energy storage can be used in renewable generation plants to store the generated energy at off-peak hours and injected back into the network at peak hours. This article explores the proper management of an energy storage system, and makes use of IoT technology to access the energy market, and the interfaces with the power distribution company. By using this technology, the power distribution company can inject the stored energy into the grid at moments high demand or in case of voltage drop, thus providing a support to the grid. A SCADA system can be used to monitor, to warn and to connect to the internet, therefore automating the system. The focus of this article is the management of the injection of the stored energy into the grid at peaks hours and voltage drops. It was used the HOMER software for the economic analyses, so that the system acts like a renewable energy plant for the power distribution company. Nevertheless, there are some regulations that be considered.

articleTitle: Development of the Occupancy Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper describes development and testing of occupancy detection system with zone temperature measurement and fire detection features. It also provides BMS connectivity via additional communication module. Described work was carried out within Milewianse project, as a part of the 4th Poland-Berlin cooperation in the field of photonics.

articleTitle: Bridge Circuit Converting Atomic Transactions Between AMBA AXI4 and AMBA AXI5 Standards
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: The PCI Express (PCIe) is a high-speed communication bus standard that offers many innovative solutions to fulfil the requirements of various systems. One of them is Atomic Operations functionality, which makes cooperation much easier in systems with multiple requesters and responders due to synchronization mechanisms that allow all elements to communicate in a non-blocking manner. The PCIe controller distributed by Cadence Design Systems uses the AMBA AXI5 standard for its implementation. However, many users of this controller still implement the older protocol standard AXI4 in their SoCs (System on Chip). To enable the use of full PCIe functionality, a converter for the AXI4 and AXI5 standards was developed. This paper describes the Bridge Circuit converting Atomic Transactions between AXI4 and AXI5 standards.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting Circuit for Wearable Battery-Free Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper presents the structure and principle of operation of a prototype low-power energy-harvesting circuit (with efficiency higher than 50 %) intended for AC-to-DC conversion, where the input signal is obtained from micro-power piezoelectric elements. The proposed electronic circuit prototype is intended to work as a wearable autonomous system that provides electrical energy obtained through mechanical vibrations in piezoelectric ceramic disks. The obtained electrical energy through a switching circuit is used to charge low-power supercapacitors. The electronic circuit consists of a bridge rectifier, a low-pass filter, a step-down (buck) synchronous converter, a power-controlling system, and a window detector to produce a power-good signal. The designed electronic circuit of the control system allows for tuning the level of the output voltage to around 1.8 V, and the output discharge current reaches values higher than 0.5 mA. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme, simulation, and experimental testing of the proposed prototype was carried out, as the obtained results confirmed the preliminary theoretical analyses and the derived analytical expressions for the basic electrical parameters.

articleTitle: Parameter Extraction from SCLC Transport Mechanism in MIS RRAM Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: In this work we study the SCLC transport mechanism in MIS RRAM structures. We extract the relevant transport parameters using an analytical model and analyze the energy distribution of traps for different temperatures. We show that using our methodology, useful parameters can be obtained that can help interpret the data and understand the physics of devices.

articleTitle: A 66dBΩ 5 GHz and 44.88 √Hz/(pA·pW) Inductorless TIA in 65 nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: High-speed optical applications demand broadband transimpedance amplifiers (TIA) for efficient current-to-voltage conversion of photodiode signals. The inherent junction capacitance of photodiodes limits TIA bandwidth. This work proposes an inductorless design strategy for broadband CMOS TIAs. To mitigate the deteriorating effect of photodiode capacitance, a cross-coupled impedance negator integrated with an auxiliary amplifier to form the modified regulated cascode structure (RGC) is utilized at the input stage and, a capacitive degeneration stage is incorporated to improve the bandwidth. The TIA is designed for a high transimpedance gain of 66 dBΩ and is implemented in standard 65nm CMOS technology. The simulation results exhibit a -3 dB bandwidth of 5 GHz, input-referred noise current of 17.74 pA/√Hz, and power consumption of 3.2 mW. This design approach renders the TIA input insensitive to the input photodiode, exhibiting a stable frequency response over a range of photodiode capacitance from 50 fF to 300 fF.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of the Functioning of the Inertial Acceleration Sensor in a Variable Temperature Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: In this research paper we delve into the behavior of inertial acceleration sensor under varying temperature conditions. Our study focuses on statistical aspects, shedding light on key parameters that characterize sensor performance. We calculate the mean acceleration values recorded by the sensor across different temperature ranges. Standard deviation quantifies the variability or dispersion of acceleration measurements. We analyze how temperature fluctuations impact this metric. A higher standard deviation may indicate increased noise or instability in sensor readings. By examining quartiles, we gain insight into the distribution of acceleration data. These quartiles help us to understand the spread of values and identify potential outliers.

articleTitle: Reflections on the First European Open Source PDK by IHP - Experiences After One Year and Future Activities
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: The IHP's open source Process Design Kit (PDK) was released to the public in February 2023, and since then significant progress has been made in its development. By making it available to a broader community, developers, researchers, and engineers can contribute their expertise, ideas, and improvements, accelerating innovation and potentially leading to breakthroughs in semiconductor technology. In this paper, we aim to share details about the current version of the Design Kit, including its features, capabilities, and the issues we encountered during the development process. We also present our collaborative development model involving multiple institutions and individuals working under the open source paradigm. This approach is still a novelty in microelectronic hardware development. In addition, we present our vision and roadmap for the PDK to inform the community and encourage further collaboration. Our goal is to explore the open source development model and promote its popularity within the microelectronics community.

articleTitle: Using Cocotb Framework During Different Stages of IC Design
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: The growing automation of integrated circuit design is both a goal and a necessity due to the expanding complexity of integrated circuit technologies. The current industry standard in this field involves employing HDL languages, such as SystemC, SystemVerilog, and VHDL, alongside verification methodologies and environments such as UVM (Universal Verification Methodology in SysteVerilog) and OVM (Open Verification Methodology in VHDL). However, the emergence of new frameworks like cocotb opens up possibilities for even greater automation and integration of the verification and testing processes, spanning from the initial stages of integrated circuit design to the final chip testing phase. The article explores the potential benefits of incorporating the cocotb framework across different stages of design and verification. This workflow not only streamlines the integrated circuit design process but also facilitates the implementation of unit test policies while alleviating the workload for designers, verification teams, and IC testing teams.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient and High-Performance Data Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: The European Chips Act signalizes the EU's strategy to not only increase domestic production capabilities but also to capture a sizable portion of the global semiconductor manufacturing market by 2030<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>. The European Chips Act aims to localize 20 % of worldwide semiconductor production to within Europe, minimizing external dependencies and reinforcing technological sovereignty. This strategic direction is crucial in tackling the severe global competition and critical supply chain vulnerabilities that recent disruptions have highlighted.

articleTitle: Practical Implementation of a Trapezoidal Waveform Generator in High Voltage SOI Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: The paper presents an introduction to the analysis of the implementation of a high-voltage trapezoidal waveform generator, starting with a schematic followed by a schematic version with overvoltage protection device set and concluding with a full layout of the latter circuit version. The consecutive design steps offer a decrease in the quality of the generator operation. This decrease is presented in relation to change of selected operation parameters of the discussed generator. Analysis outcome and a scenario of further steps of the design analysis is proposed.

articleTitle: Exploring Photonic Integrated Circuits - Technologies, Applications and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: During the presentation, we will explore the technologies and applications of integrated photonic circuits, focusing on global development challenges, trends, and opportunities. We will also highlight Poland's technical and technological potential and perspectives on the Polish photonic industry.

articleTitle: Memory Protection with Cached Authentication Trees
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: Protecting system's memory was researched in the past, and there are several methods of achieving it such as memory encryption, memory hashes, and message authentication codes. To overcome associated performance overhead, authentication tree designs have been proposed, for example, well known Merkle tree, TEC-tree or dynamic authentication tree (DAT). This work builds on the top of the DAT design by integrating tree node caches and evaluating the improved viability of the approach. Our cached design was implemented on a Xilinx Zynq-7020 APSoC with a hard core CPU communicating with the fabric-based memory protection controller. The addition of caches to the dynamic authentication tree design increased the performance enough to be competitive with TEC-Tree, and in scenarios that frequently access previously processed data, the cache-added DAT was able to outperform TEC-Tree based designs.

articleTitle: Employing Parallelization Technique to Reduce Area and Power in a Booth Encoded Algorithm-Based Multiplier
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper discusses the improvement of the multiplication operation speed in multipliers based on Booth's algorithm. The main goal of Booth's algorithm is to reduce the number of partial products by half, as a result of which, the multiplication operation will be completed sooner. The method proposed in this paper to solve this problem is designing a parallel multiplier using only one Booth Encoder circuit and one adder circuit. With the help of a series of circuits and control signals, these two circuits work in parallel and simultaneously so that the speed of the multiplication operation is not affected much. The production of partial products and their accumulation is being done in parallel. At the same time, the amount of hardware that is directly related to the power consumption is significantly reduced. The presented design is implemented in CMOS technology and 0.18um process. The proposed multiplier produces the correct output after 78nsec, and its operating speed is 12.8 MHz. The average power consumption of this multiplier is approximately 1.09 mW, and the number of transistors required for its construction is 2927.

articleTitle: Advanced Silicon Technologies: Design Consequences of Scaling Solutions for Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: Despite multiple roadblocks and 'red-brick” walls identified on its path, the Moore's Law continues towards single Angstrom digits, promising further improvements in device density and energy efficiency. FinFET and Nanosheet technologies bring 3-rd dimension to device design, and new back-side power rail schemes decouple power delivery from signal lines. All those new technology solutions change the way the circuits and products are designed, manufactured, packaged, and tested. This paper reviews the impact the technology scaling has on various components of SoC and their designs.

articleTitle: LLVM Library for a Dedicated Processor Instruction Set – A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper discusses the LLVM compilation environment, which restricts machine instruction outputs to a single value. This assumption poses challenges when dealing with non-typical destination processors. Therefore, we present an extension to overcome this limitation, enabling multivalued outputs for machine instructions.

articleTitle: Sub-terahertz Near-field Dielectric Sensor in CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: In this article, we present a label-free near-field sensor designed for sensing and spectroscopy within an aqueous environment operating in the sub-terahertz frequency range. Fabricated using standard silicon complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology, the sensor addresses a pressing need in modern science and technology for compact, cost-effective, end-user-friendly devices.

articleTitle: Numerical Test for Stability Evaluation of Analog Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: In this contribution, a new numerical test for the stability evaluation of analog circuits is presented. Usually, if an analog circuit is unstable then the roots of its characteristic equation are localized on the right half-plane of the Laplace s- plane. Because this region is unbounded, we employ the bilinear transformation to map it into the unit disc on the complex plane. Hence, the existence of any root inside the unit disc implies circuit instability. In our test, we employ the global roots and poles finding algorithm based on phase analysis to detect the roots of the characteristic equation inside the unit disc. Unlike other stability tests, our approach allows one to evaluate the stability of analog circuits and systems whose characteristic equations are not polynomials. In order to demonstrate its efficiency, generality and applicability, we analyze a memristor-based chaotic circuit whose stability depends on the value of the fractional-order parameter. The proposed test correctly detects the parameter ranges of either stability or instability for the considered analog circuit.

articleTitle: Utilizing a Variable Activation Threshold Approach to Calculate and Increase Probabilities of Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: In this paper, a variable activation threshold method for increasing the probabilities of anomaly detection is described. The method has been implemented in an intrusion detection system (IDS) based on artificial immune systems (AIS). The proposed method involves decreasing the size of the activation threshold bit by bit to increase the size of the receptor set and in turn, extend receptor coverage for more successful anomaly detection. Equations for calculating anomaly detection probabilities using the proposed method are presented and tested against experimental results to verify their usability, and the work is then concluded.

articleTitle: A 66 $\mu \mathrm{W}$ Asynchronous Time-Domain Bulk-Tuned Offset Cancellation Circuit for High-Precision Dynamic Comparator
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel asynchronous high-precision, low-power, time-domain bulk-tuned offset cancellation technique for high-speed dynamic comparator. The proposed offset cancellation technique minimizes the offset by using bulk-tuning in conjunction with offset sampling in the time domain. The proposed phase detector eliminates the dead zone and is symmetric to both outputs. An energy and area-efficient charge pump with offset polarity-based selectivity is also introduced. The proposed offset cancellation scheme is implemented in 65-nm CMOS technology with a 1.2 V supply, and analytical modeling of the time difference of comparator outputs and offset is also presented. The proposed design has a power consumption of 65.8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{W}$</tex> and maintains a calibration speed of 1 GHz with the comparator operating at 2 GHz frequency. The standard deviation of the offset is decreased to 33.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{V}$</tex> from 2.183 mV, qualifying it for high-speed, high-precision applications.

articleTitle: General-Purpose High Swing Digital-to-Analog Converter for Low Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: A moderate-resolution Digital-To-Analog Converter (DAC) specifically crafted for general-purpose use in a wide range of applications within a single integrated circuit. This paper presents the development of a 10-bit DAC in 22 nm. FD-SOI technology. The main goals for the proposed DAC are high output swing, low power consumption, and a minimized die area while keeping the device inherently monotonic. The simulation shows a total power consumption of 0.9 mW at Nyquist frequency, with expected static linearity better than 0.32 LSB and 0.22 LSB for integral (INL) and differential (DNL) nonlinearities respectively. Effective Number of Bits (ENOB) of 9.5 bits with Spurious Free Dynamic Range (SFDR) of 65.9 dBc at Nyquist. The circuit performs well for low-frequency signals with an update rate of 20, while the Nyquist rate operates at half of this value.

articleTitle: 10-Bit ADC SAR with Passive Charge Redistribution in 40nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation results of a 10-bit successive approximation analog-to-digital converter with passive charge redistribution. The design was realized in CMOS 40nm process and is foreseen for multichannel measurement integrated circuits. The main requirement of the presented design was ultra low power consumption and small area occupancy, which would allow for placing independent converter in each input channel. The paper describes in-detail the converter operation principle and design solutions that aimed at on-chip implementation.

articleTitle: Jitter Minimization of Phase-locked Loops for OFDM-Based Millimeter-Wave Communication Systems with Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: Phased-lock loop rms phase jitter is modelled for millimeter-wave (mmWave) OFDM systems. Emphasis is placed on phased arrays for fast beam steering. A cascade of at least two phase-locked loops (PLL) is proposed, where a slow PLL with programmable output frequency in the lower GHz range drives one or more fast integer-N mmWave PLLs with separate digital phase control. The large loop bandwidth of the latter reduces its phase noise contribution from the voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) and reduces the switching time of the PLL phase to below 100 ns. The crucial point in the optimization of the loop bandwidths is the anticipation of the phase noise reduction in the receiver, after the OFDM signal has been down-converted to the baseband. As a result, a low rms phase jitter can be combined with ultra-short phase switching times. The corresponding signal-to-noise ratio at the receiver output after common phase error correction is deduced from the PLL phase noise spectra, the number of PLLs in the phased array, and the sub carrier spacing.

articleTitle: Study of Storage Capacity of Charge Trap EAROM NAND Memory Designed for Integration with VeSTIC Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper presents a study of increased information storage capabilities of single memory cell of new 3D design. Memory was designed for integration with VeSTIC (Vertical Slit Transistor-based Integrated Circuits) technology, to increase the circuit density to effectively use available space. This memory operates in relative environment, with control voltage not exceeding 9 V. Test simulations of memory cell indicate, that it has the capability to hold even more than 2 bits of information data. This design opens new possibilities for integration of advanced integrated circuits with dedicated non-volatile memory in a single chip with maximum device density.

articleTitle: Predicting the Workload of the Repair Department in a Company Producing Electronic Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: During the production of electronic modules tests of the correctness of individual production stages are carried out at many points of the production line. Modules that do not meet the test requirements are sent for repair. Depending on the number of modules produced, their complexity and production volume, the burden on the repair department changes. To ensure ongoing repairs of the damaged modules, it is necessary to ensure appropriate repair teams. This paper proposes an algorithm for predicting the number of modules that will require repairs in particular weeks. The correct operation of this algorithm was verified on the example of the real data from a company producing such modules. The obtained research results were commented on.

articleTitle: Analysis of an Influence of the Colour of the Emitted Light on Dynamic Properties of Power LEDs
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper presents the results of experimental research illustrating an influence of the colour of the emitted light on dynamic electrical and optical properties of the power LEDs. The used measurement setup and the tested devices are described. The dynamic model of a power LED is proposed. Some results of the computations and measurements are presented and discussed. The investigations are performed for 4 LEDs made by the same manufacturer, mounted in the same cases and characterized by the same maximum allowable value of the forward current. Both the turn-on and turn-off times resulting from electrical inertia are measured and discussed, as well as such times resulting from optical inertia.

articleTitle: Design of a DC Nano-Grid Based on DBS and Smart Variable Load Control Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: In this paper, an island, DC Nano-grid, is studied. It operates independently and does not have access to the national power grid so that it can be used for remote locations. The plan considers both supply-side management and demand-side management by prioritizing resources, including renewable sources (photovoltaic array and wind turbine), energy storage (battery) and non-renewable sources (diesel generator). Also, the separation of loads into sensitive and insensitive loads and priority for sensitive loads are designed so that while maintaining the system's reliability and creating a balance between consumption and production, economic and environmental issues are also considered. In addition, it tries to use the most exploited sources of electricity generation with the lowest cost (renewable sources). A hybrid distributed control method (DC BUS SIGNALING) controls the Nano-grid, in which the voltage drop is created in the DC bus (Voltage drop method) to control sources and loads. The paper's primary goal is to implement a controller to keep the DC bus voltage at a reasonable level in the presence of constant and variable loads and prevent excessive voltage drop.

articleTitle: A Method Supporting Hardware Implementation of Vector Quantization Module in HoG Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: In this work, we dealt with topics related to computer vision, with particular focus on solutions aimed at ensuring computational efficiency. One of the algorithms often used in computer vision is Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HoG), often used in object detection in video sequences. In many applications, this algorithm should be able to run in real time, simultaneously on devices with low computing power. In this work, we attempted to implement one of its key stages at the level of digital specialized circuits (also suitable for integrated circuit realization). At this stage, it is determined which of the bins the vector calculated on the basis of previously calculated gradients for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y$</tex> coordinates belongs to. We presented solutions for different numbers of bins, but also solutions that can be considered more general, i.e. allowing to change the number of bins.

articleTitle: CMOS Computational Structures Using a Nonlinear Multifunctional Core
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: Signal processing circuits represent an important class of CMOS structures, finding a multitude of applications: neural networks, portable equipments, wireless nanosensors, communications and medical implantable devices. The analog implementation of these circuits can improve their performances, the low-power operation, reduced silicon area and increased processing speed representing the most important advantages. We will present a new approach of designing analog signal processing circuits, introducing the new concept of multifunctional structures (computational circuits that use the same functional core in order to obtain multiple linear and nonlinear circuit functions). The efficiency of the proposed design technique will be illustrated for obtaining high performances fundamental analog signal processing circuits: transconductance amplifiers, voltage multipliers, squaring blocks, active resistor structures and function synthesizer circuits. The estimated theoretical results confirm by specific simulations.

articleTitle: Device for Simultaneous Recording of Lung Parameters and ECG as a Universal Tool for Comprehensive Physiological Monitoring - A Developmental Model
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: The device, in the form of a chest strap, has been developed to reliably record electrocardiography (ECG) signals and respiratory waveforms with high precision. Understanding the interaction of these signals can help assess cardiovascular capability and intravascular volume status. The application-friendly measurement of ECG and respiratory waveforms using the same dry electrodes demonstrates the utility of simultaneously recording such signals for comprehensive physiological monitoring. Preliminary tests of the device under practical conditions were conducted with 5 healthy adult individuals. The results, in the form of recorded waveforms during moderate exercise, confirm the easy and unobtrusive application for use in both home and hospital settings. Simultaneous recording of ECG and respiratory waveform signals, as well as chest hydration, can contribute significant information when monitoring patients in a clinical setting as well as when using telemedicine methods in a home setting.

articleTitle: Digital Fuzzy Logic Controller with Scalable Sequential Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a digital CMOS integrated circuit implementing a fuzzy logic controller. The proposed architecture is suitable for serial processing of membership functions and fuzzy rules. The parameterised VHDL model allows to synthesise the programmable circuit of the required size for a particular application. The impact of selected model parameters on speed, occupied area and power dissipation is also discussed.

articleTitle: Identification and Optimization of Landmarks on the Impedance Cardiography Signal ICG
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: By proper processing of signals, it is possible to eliminate interference, improve data quality, and obtain more accurate information. In the field of diagnostic medicine and patient monitoring, appropriate signal preparation is essential for correctly interpreting results and making sound clinical decisions. The aim of this study is to present the influence of modifying selected averaging parameters on the generation of the ensemble average of ICG signal. A comparison of ensemble average was conducted considering recordings of 20s and 40s in the range of 1–17 average complexes. The results indicate that the quantity of average complexes should be precisely specified and optimized to ensure globally comparable results.

articleTitle: Simulation, Measurements and Analysis of the CMOS Temperature Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper describes a CMOS temperature sensor, focusing on measurements and analysis of selected aspects of its performance. The measurements showed high thermal linearity of the scrutined sensor. Measurements include not only the sensor's performance for large temperature ranges by testing it in a thermal chamber, but also by attempted use of the electrothermal filter and ESD structures placed near the sensor as heating elements. In addition, the response of the temperature sensor and electrothermal filter to visible and near-visible irradiation was studied, providing interesting results.

articleTitle: On-Chip Infrastructure for Mission-Mode Monitoring of Aero-Space Applications: Towards Silicon Lifecycle Management; Embedded Tutorial
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This tutorial summarizes the on-chip cross-layer infrastructure such as sensors and monitors under development at IHP Microelectronics. This infrastructure deals with detecting single-event upset (SEU) in flip-flops, single-event transient (SET) in combinational logic, monitoring power-bus activity and electronics aging evolution. At a higher level, this infrastructure allows detecting faults that affect the real-time operating system (RTOS) activity in a mixed-criticality environment (i.e., faults that affect the task scheduling process by violating execution deadline, time and space allocated for critical tasks under execution). This infrastructure can be used for on-chip analytics to predict in-flight SEU rate. Such solution enables mission-mode monitoring of system operation, which is a critical aspect of silicon lifecycle management (SLM) framework. Currently, this on-chip infrastructure is being implemented in different versions of a RISC-V processor. Such design is based on the IHP's CMOS 130nm rad-hard technology.

articleTitle: Application of Imagery Modeling and Deep Learning in Chip Thermal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: Currently, with the reduction of transistor size and the increase in the number of transistors on the chip, thermal simulation in the chip design process has become increasingly important. Thermal simulation can predict the working conditions and temperature of chips in the early stages, providing valuable feedback for chip design to ensure the optimal working temperature. Currently, thermal simulation software typically faces challenges of higher accuracy and longer computation time. The use of deep learning methods helps to quickly obtain high-precision thermal simulation results, which helps to shorten chip design time and accelerate the chip design process. The purpose of the Deep Learning based chip thermal analysis method proposed in this article is not only to verify the feasibility of using deep learning in chip thermal analysis, but also to reduce the time used for thermal simulation in the chip design process and ultimately accelerate the entire chip design process. The experimental dataset is the temperature of multiple layouts of a chip, and using mature image processing deep learning models, high-precision predictions can be achieved.

articleTitle: Truth Table Based Intelligent Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: Computing architectures for solving design and test problems and managing social processes based on monitoring and vector logical processing of big data as addresses are considered. A model of data structures in the form of a truth table is considered for solving combinatorial problems associated with technical diagnostics, monitoring, and control of cyber-physical and cyber-social space. The problem of transferring the von Neumann architecture into memory and replacing a powerful processor by read-write transactions on logical vectors to reduce energy and latency when simulation logical functionality of any dimension is considered. A truth table is proposed to describe the tested combinations of faults on the input lines. Representing functionality in the form of a structure of smaller elements reduces the memory for storing logical vectors by introducing connections between elements but complicates the simulation algorithm and increases the processing time of the logical circuit. Logic vector functionality from n-inputs has the advantage of simulating more input variables in parallel in a single clock cycle. If there are no memory restrictions, then representing the functionality as a single logical vector is more time efficient and simpler for the algorithm for in-memory simulation, as well as for executing functions in production. Therefore, the use of a logical vector instead of the structure of typical technological elements is a definite step towards smart data structures in-memory computing. If the speed of read-write transactions on memory approaches the performance of logic circuits in the processor, then the next step in the electronic technology market will be the transition from processor logic to vector logic in in-memory computing. Smart data structures for fault-free simulation are represented by a superposition of logical vectors of functionality included in the digital circuit. Examples are given of processing big data as truth table addresses for constructing a vector logical model of a social process.

articleTitle: Leveraging Lookup Tables for Efficient LDO Design Exploration using Open-Source CAD Tools and IHP-Open130-G2 PDK
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: In this paper, the design space exploration through analog circuit automation techniques using the IHP open source PDK is presented. The proposed workflow is focused on the realization of integrated LDOs, which are essential building blocks for power tree generation in modern integrated circuits. Our approach includes a simplified analytical derivation and the use of precomputed lookup tables that allow to extract the best trade-offs from the design space obtained. Additionally, the modular implementation allows to integrate pre-designed building blocks to the analysis, at the cost of the ability to co-design the different parts of the LDO system. This work is an initial step towards the generation of basic assisting blocks intended for energy-efficient ASICs implemented in the IHP open source technology.

articleTitle: A System for Measuring Physiological Parameters During Extreme Activities
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: The paper presents the tenets for a proprietary system consisting of specialized mobile measurement modules which will consist of specialized mobile measurement modules for measuring physiological parameters during extreme activities. Extreme activities refer to any physical effort that involves high levels of risk, intensity and adrenaline, such as mountain climbing, deep-sea diving, skydiving, endurance racing and, in particular, piloting military aircraft. Measuring physiological parameters during extreme activities is of crucial importance for the health and safety of those taking part in them. These parameters include heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen saturation, body temperature, respiratory rate and carotid flow. Monitoring these parameters enables the early detection of any abnormalities or signs of distress, along with appropriate intervention if necessary. In the introduction, the aspect related to monitoring physiological parameters during extreme activities is discussed, and the potential risks and challenges associated with such activities are stressed, with particular emphasis on piloting the aircraft. Then the physiological systems (including cardiovascular, respiratory and musculoskeletal systems) of importance due to the changes that occur in the pilot's body during the flight are identified. The architecture of the proprietary measurement system and individual modules as well as their proposed placement on the subject's body are discussed. The paper also outlines the specific requirements for solutions dedicated to measuring physiological parameters during extreme activities, such as liquid ingress protection, shock resistance, battery life, data transmission without fault or guaranteeing continuous measurement. The conclusion highlights the future prospects and potential applications of the developed modules while military pilots perform extreme manoeuvres.

articleTitle: Single Dopant Lithography for the Fabrication of Atomic-scale Devices and Quantum Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: We describe approaches for the fabrication of single atom electronic devices and of devices with spin-based qubits for quantum computing. Single ion implantation is one of the main candidates for fabricating atomic-scale devices. Here, the ability to precisely locate single dopant atoms has the potential to enable deterministic, tunable control over key electronic and magneto-optical properties of the basic devices necessary for solid-state quantum computing. Further, the electrical operation of a CMOS compatible single dopant atom device operating at room-temperature (RT) is presented. It is based on a single dopant atom quantum dot (QD) transistor using phosphorous atoms isolated within nanoscale SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>tunnel barriers. In contrast to single dopant transistors in silicon, where the QD potential well is shallow and device operation limited to ~1 K temperatures, here, a deep (~1eV) potential well allows electron confinement even at RT [1]. This suggests higher temperature operation, at ~10 K or greater if needed, for quantum electronic circuits. The transistors, based on ~10 nm size scale Si/SiO2/Si point-contact tunnel junctions defined by scanning probe lithography and ‘geometric oxidation’ of the point-contact region, have enabled the control of single [1], and double tunnel coupled QDs [2], and investigations of single particle thermodynamics in a Maxwell ‘demon’ configuration [3].

articleTitle: AI Algorithms for Plasma Particle Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: Detecting micron-sized particles is crucial for analyzing complex plasmas, with machine learning and artificial intelligence algorithms showing significant advancements over classical methods. This study employs architectures for detecting and tracking particles in the Plasmakristallexperiment 4 (PK-4). Given the constraints of parabolic flight experiments, the research explores optimized, less complex models to balance efficiency and accuracy. Comparative analysis is conducted identifying the most effective approach for application to PK-4 experimental data.

articleTitle: Sub-terahertz Si CMOS Based Emitters and Detectors
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This paper presents compact CMOS-based electronic sources and detectors designed for the sub-terahertz frequency range. We illustrate that achievable noise-equivalent power levels, in the range of a few tens of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{pW}/\sqrt{}\text{Hz}$</tex>, along with emitted power reaching up to 100 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{W}$</tex> ‘, enable the construction of effective quasi-optical emitter-detector pairs operating within the 200 - 266 GHz range. Additionally, the input power-related signal-to-noise ratio can reach up to 70 dB for a one Hz equivalent noise bandwidth. We showcase the versatility of these compact devices across various applications, including imaging, spectroscopy, and wireless communication links.

articleTitle: FSMLock: Sequential Logic Locking Through Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: FSMLock is a new sequential logic locking technique that utilizes classical cryptographic block cipher algorithms to conceal and restrict access to the targeted finite state machine (FSM). Unlike other FSM-based sequential logic locking techniques, FSMLock adds no additional states to the state transition graph (STG). Instead, FSMLock is applied to a sequential circuit by abstracting a flattened version of its distinct state entry table (SET) into a binary data file, which can then be encrypted and stored in non-volatile memory (NVM). The encrypted flattened stats entry table (FSET) information is read in partitions such that, at run-time, only a subset of the sequential logic is in scope. The resulting architecture has a theoretical resistance against removal attacks, circuit unrolling-based satisfiability (SAT) attacks, and topological/boolean functional analysis attacks. This is due to the SAT-hard abstraction as an encrypted binary data file of the locked circuitry.

articleTitle: Real-time Detection of Pathogens in Hydroalcoholic Solutions during Hand Disinfection Process
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: As we learned from the COVID-19 pandemic, hand hygiene is a crucial barrier for the limitation of infection outbreaks, especially in sensitive areas such as hospitals. Any sensor able to generate early alerts in case of contamination risk is therefore of great interest for public healthcare. Among the different technologies already explored for bacterial identification, impedance spectroscopy is one of the easiest to implement and to integrate inside everyday devices. However, bacterial identification by impedance spectroscopy is generally carried out in an aqueous medium, i.e. conductive solution, and with microelectrodes whose size is adapted to the size of the bacteria. In this paper, we demonstrate that it is possible to perform measurements directly in a hydroalcoholic medium, i.e. non-conductive solution, and with millimeter-scale electrodes, which are less expensive to produce and easier to integrate in any medical device. The results show that when a sample contains bacteria, even at low concentrations, the impedance spectrum of the hydroalcoholic solution is significantly altered. This result is an important proof of concept for the development of hand disinfectant dispensers capable of analyzing hand-washing residues in real-time and of raising alerts when samples contain an unusual quantity of bacteria.

articleTitle: Myasthenia Gravis Disease Diagnosis System
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: The article presents the design and implementation of an information system to support the diagnosis and follow-up of symptoms resulting from Myasthenia Gravis (MG) disease. MG belongs to a group of rare diseases, the diagnosis of which requires a special approach. The presented system makes it possible to examine the patient, and then using various algorithms analyzes the collected data. The innovative, proprietary algorithm is a procedure for detecting the symptom of drooping eyelid (ptosis), which uses automatic detection of the patient's face, and then analyzes eyelid movements. Another test is the assessment of arm muscle performance. Based on the video recorded during a patient examination, system automatically recognized drooping of the arms. The system is being tested at the Clinic of Neurology in Poznan, Poland and at a hospital in Bydgoszcz, Poland.

articleTitle: Preface
publicationTitle: 2024 31st International Conference on Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and System (MIXDES)
abstract: This monograph presents recent works on micro- and nanoelectronics design methods, modelling, simulation, testing and manufacturing technology in diverse areas including embedded systems, MEMS, sensors, actuators, power devices and biomedical applications. It contains the selected submissions related to the topics discussed during the 31st International Conference “Mixed Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems” - MIXDES 2024 (June 27 - 28, 2024, Gdańsk, Poland).
